questions.question: Posters, signs, and stickers on the windshield and windows:

options.text: Are a fun way to personalize your vehicle.
Are allowed if they do not block your view.
Are not allowed, unless the law requires them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are not allowed, unless the law requires them.
questions.explanation: You cannot put anything on your windows. No sign, poster, or sticker may be placed on any vehicle window, unless the law specifically requires it to be there.

questions.question: As you approach the top of a hill, you should:

options.text: Speed up a little.
Be ready to stop if needed.
Keep the same speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: You cannot see what is on the other side of a hill or around a curve. A vehicle could be stopped just out of sight. You must be able to stop. Slow down when you reach a hill or curve so you can stop if necessary.

questions.question: When leaving the interstate, you should start to slow down:

options.text: When you turn on your blinker to enter the exit lane.
When you see a sign for your exit.
After you turn into the exit lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: After you turn into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Stay at highway speed while you are on the main road. Do not slow down until you enter the exit lane.

questions.question: A broken yellow centerline means:

options.text: You cannot pass.
You can pass on the right when the road ahead is clear.
You can pass on the left when the road ahead is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass on the left when the road ahead is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow centerline means you can cross it to pass another vehicle on the left if there is no oncoming traffic. Never cross a solid yellow centerline to pass.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
Merge.
Road curves ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided red sign means stop.

questions.question: When driving at night, you should:

options.text: Always use high beams.
Look directly at oncoming headlights.
Keep a greater distance from the car ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a greater distance from the car ahead.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous because you cannot see as well. You cannot judge speed and distance as easily. Keep a larger gap between you and the car ahead. This helps you stop if it stops suddenly. Use your headlights correctly at night.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, move back to your original lane when:

options.text: You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
You have passed the front bumper of the other vehicle.
You are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Only move back to your lane when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your mirror. This makes sure you have enough room to safely get in front of the other vehicle.

questions.question: Looking far ahead while driving on the highway:

options.text: Helps you keep up with traffic.
Helps you avoid sudden braking or turning.
Helps you spot police officers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps you avoid sudden braking or turning.
questions.explanation: Look far ahead so you can be ready to stop or change lanes without rushing. This makes you safer, saves fuel, and keeps traffic moving smoothly.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No turns allowed.
No dead end.
No U-turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turns.
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed. You often see this sign at intersections with heavy oncoming traffic.

questions.question: You are driving on a one-way street. You can turn left onto another one-way street only if:

options.text: You speed up before turning.
Traffic on that street flows to the right.
Traffic on that street flows to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic on that street flows to the left.
questions.explanation: You can turn left onto a one-way street where traffic flows to the left if no sign prevents it. You cannot turn left onto a one-way street where traffic flows to the right.

questions.question: You drive defensively when you:

options.text: Keep one car length between you and the car ahead.
Look only at the car in front of you while driving.
Keep your eyes moving to watch for hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your eyes moving to watch for hazards.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means looking ahead for possible hazards. Staring only at the road directly in front of your car is dangerous. Scan the road ahead and stay aware of vehicles around you.

questions.question: How do stopping distances and crash severity change with speed?

options.text: They decrease as speed increases.
They are not affected by speed.
They increase as speed increases.

questions.correctAnswerText: They increase as speed increases.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds cause serious problems. As speed increases, stopping distance gets longer and crashes become more severe. This increases the risk of injury and death. Leave more space between cars when you drive faster so you can stop safely if needed.

questions.question: You should always travel at:

options.text: The speed of the vehicles around you.
The speed limit.
A speed that fits the road and weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: A speed that fits the road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: Your speed should match the road conditions, weather, and speed limit. Never drive faster than the speed limit. Slow down when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: You are in the left lane of a two-lane road and many cars are passing you on the right. A driver behind you wants to go faster. What should you do?

options.text: Stay in your lane to not slow traffic.
Drive onto the left shoulder to let cars pass.
Move to the right lane when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Use the left lane for faster driving, passing, and turning left. Use the right lane for slower speeds, entering the road, and turning right.

questions.question: Why should you increase your distance behind a large vehicle?

options.text: To see around the sides of the vehicle.
Because drivers tend to pass large vehicles from behind.
Because the vehicle's slipstream will affect your car.

questions.correctAnswerText: To see around the sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Drivers of large vehicles like trucks, buses, and trailers cannot see you if you drive directly behind them. Stay farther back to see around the vehicle and watch the road ahead.

questions.question: You park downhill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way do you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: When parking facing downhill on any road, turn your wheels toward the edge of the road. This way, if your brakes fail, your car rolls away from traffic. When parking uphill on a road without a curb, also turn toward the road edge. On a road with a curb facing uphill, turn toward the center so the car rolls into the curb.

questions.question: In which situation should your wheels not point straight ahead?

options.text: When waiting to turn left at a traffic light.
When parked on a hill or sloped driveway.
When parked on a level roadside with no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When parked on a hill or sloped driveway.
questions.explanation: When waiting to turn left, keep your wheels straight. If hit from behind, this prevents you from sliding into oncoming traffic. When parked on a slope, turn your wheels so your car won't roll into traffic if brakes fail.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow centerline mean?

options.text: Passing is not allowed.
You can pass on the right when the road is clear.
You can pass on the left when the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass on the left when the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow centerline on your side means you can cross it to pass when the road ahead is clear.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not drink and drive.
Slippery when wet.
Road curves ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black text. They alert you to upcoming dangers. This sign warns that the road becomes slippery when wet.

questions.question: For drivers 21 or older, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:

options.text: 0.05 percent or higher.
0.08 percent or higher.
0.02 percent or higher.

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent or higher.
questions.explanation: For drivers 21 and older, driving with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is illegal. Driving under the influence is both illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: You are driving at the speed limit when a traffic light turns yellow. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and go through the intersection without being careful.
Speed up to cross before the light turns red.
Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the red light is coming soon. Stop if you can do so safely. If you cannot stop safely, cross the intersection carefully.

questions.question: What is the speed limit on interstate highways when no other speed limit is posted?

options.text: 55 mph
65 mph
75 mph

questions.correctAnswerText: 65 mph
questions.explanation: The speed limit on interstate highways is 65 miles per hour. Always follow posted speed limits if they are different.

questions.question: You want to enter the freeway but there is no gap in traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Keep your speed and force other drivers to make room.
Slow down on the ramp and wait for a gap.
Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a gap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down on the ramp and wait for a gap.
questions.explanation: Slow down on the ramp to wait for a safe gap. If you stop at the end of the ramp, you will not have enough space to speed up before entering the freeway.

questions.question: When should you give up your right-of-way?

options.text: Often, even at traffic lights.
Whenever it helps prevent crashes.
Never. It confuses other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whenever it helps prevent crashes.
questions.explanation: Do not assume other drivers will give you the right-of-way. Give up your right-of-way whenever it helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: Which factor affects how fast a person absorbs alcohol?

options.text: Weight
Height
Intelligence

questions.correctAnswerText: Weight
questions.explanation: A person's weight affects how fast they absorb alcohol. Other factors include biological sex, food in the stomach, and how many drinks they have had. Time is the only way to remove alcohol from the body.

questions.question: When is highway pavement most slippery?

options.text: After it has been raining for several hours
When rain first starts
After it has been raining for one to two hours

questions.correctAnswerText: When rain first starts
questions.explanation: Pavement is most slippery when rain first begins. Dirt and oil on the road mix with water and create a slick coating.

questions.question: At what speed can a car hydroplane on wet roads?

options.text: 45 miles per hour
35 miles per hour
40 miles per hour

questions.correctAnswerText: 35 miles per hour
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning can happen at speeds as low as 35 mph. At 35 mph and below, tires can move water away. At higher speeds, tires cannot move water away as well, and the car may ride on top of the water like water skis.

questions.question: What must you do when you see a flashing red light at an intersection?

options.text: Stop completely, check for other traffic and pedestrians, then go if safe.
Slow down and go carefully.
Stop and stay stopped as long as the light is red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, check for other traffic and pedestrians, then go if safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, look for other traffic and pedestrians, and proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: Where are U-turns not allowed?

options.text: In a parking lot
On or near curves or hills
On a straight road where you can see 500 feet ahead in both directions

questions.correctAnswerText: On or near curves or hills
questions.explanation: Never make a U-turn on or near a curve or hill. You cannot see oncoming traffic or pedestrians and could cause a crash.

questions.question: Which road is most likely to be slippery in cold weather after snow or rain?

options.text: A hilly, open road
A residential road
A road in a shaded area

questions.correctAnswerText: A road in a shaded area
questions.explanation: Shaded areas on the road freeze before other areas and thaw after other areas. On cold, wet days, watch for ice in shaded spots.
